newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power continues higher in cold snap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power continues higher in cold snap.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Midwest rose again Tuesday as a cold snap gripped much of the area and a nuclear power unit tripped off line in Minnesota, brokers and marketers said.
Temperatures through much of Minnesota and North Dakota were expected to reach highs of only the mid-20s degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday, with the same or even colder weather forecast for Wednesday.
The cold weather was forecast to last through most of the week.

In Minnesota, Northern States Power's 544 megawatt (MW) Monticello nuclear power plant was expected to resume full power production by late Wednesday after tripping off line early this morning due to an operator error, the company said.
Also, Northern States 169 megawatt High Bridge coal-fired unit 6 was out of service for maintenance, with no restart date set.

Separately, Union Electric was attempting to restart its 1,125 megawatt Callaway nuclear power plant in Fulton, Mo. early Tuesday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said, but sources said the unit was not producing power Tuesday afternoon.
Union Electric would not comment on the status of the plant, but said it expected to issue a press release regarding Callaway Tuesday.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were talked at $33.00-37.00 with some offers said as high as $40 per megawatt hour (MWh).

With the high MAPP prices some marketers were reported to be staying out of the market, making trade relatively thin, but others were reported to be reeling in power from across the U.S. to take advantage of the high values.
Next-day MAPP power was talked near $30.00 on Monday.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were notionally assessed steady in the $8.50-10.00 area.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), the cold weather demand pushed non-firm peak next day power prices to the $30.00-35.00 range from $29.00-34.00 on Monday, the traders said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday delivery were reported relatively steady to higher at $27.00-29.50 with some offers said to be as high as $32.00, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was said to be little changed in thin trade at $12.50-14.00 per MWh.
December peak ECAR was talked steady in the $19.60-20.00 range, while January/February ECAR was assessed at $21.60-22.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Wednesday were talked steady in the $27.00-31.00 range, the sources said.
